translations.text: Paul, an apostle not from men nor through men, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised him from the dead,
and all the brothers who are with me, to the churches of Galatia:
grace to you and peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ,
who gave himself for our sins, so that he might deliver us from this present evil world, by the will of our God and Father,
to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
I am amazed that you are turning away so quickly from him who called you by the grace of Christ, to another gospel,
which is not another at all; but there are some who are troubling you and want to pervert the gospel of Christ.
But even if we, or an angel from heaven, should preach to you a gospel other than the one we preached to you, let him be accursed!
As I said before, so now I say again: if anyone preaches to you a gospel other than the one we preached to you, let him be accursed!
Am I now trying to win over men, or God? Or am I seeking to please men? If I were still pleasing men, I would not be a servant of Christ.
I make known to you, brothers, that the gospel which was preached to you by me is not of human origin.
For I did not receive it from a man, nor was I taught it, but it came through a revelation of Jesus Christ.
For you have heard of my former way of life in Judaism, how I persecuted the churches of God beyond measure and ravaged them.
And I advanced in Judaism beyond many of my own age among my people, being far more zealous for the teachings of my fathers.
But when it pleased God, who set me apart from my mother's womb and called me by his grace,
to reveal his Son through me, so that I might preach him among the Gentiles, I did not immediately consult with flesh and blood,
nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me, but I went to Arabia and then returned again to Damascus.
Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to see Cephas, and I stayed with him fifteen days.
I saw none of the other apostles, except James, the brother of the Lord.
As for what I am writing to you, behold, before God, I am not lying.
Then I went again into the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
And I was unknown by face to the churches of Judea that were in Christ;
they only heard it said that he who once persecuted us now preaches the faith that he once ravaged.
And they glorified God because of me.
Then again, in the fourteenth year, I went up to Jerusalem with Barnabas; I took Titus along with me as well.

And I went up because of a revelation, and I set before them the gospel that I preach among the Gentiles. But I did this privately, with those who were held in esteem, in case I might be running, or had run, in vain.
But not even Titus, who was with me, was compelled to be circumcised, although he was a Gentile.
This was because of the false brothers who had slipped in. They came in to spy on our freedom, which I have through Christ Jesus, so that they might enslave us.
We did not give in and submit to them even for one hour, so that the truth of the gospel might remain with you.

But as for those who were thought to be something: whatever they once were makes no difference to me. God does not show partiality to a person. For those who were held in esteem added nothing further to what I said.
On the contrary, they recognized that the gospel for the uncircumcised had been entrusted to me, just as the gospel for the circumcised had been entrusted to Peter.
For the one who helped Peter in his apostleship to the circumcised also helped me in mine to the Gentiles.

And when they recognized the grace that had been given to me, James, Cephas and John, who regarded themselves as pillars, gave me and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship, so that we would go to the Gentiles and they would go to the circumcised.
They asked only that we remember the poor, which was the very thing we were eager to do.
And when Peter came to Antioch, I opposed him to his face, because he was in the wrong.
For before certain people came from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles. But when they came, he drew back and kept himself apart, because he was afraid of those of the circumcision.
And the other Jews joined him in this hypocrisy, so that even Barnabas was carried away by their hypocrisy.

But when I saw that they were not walking straight according to the truth of the gospel, I said to Peter in front of everyone: "If you, a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how can you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?"
We are Jews by birth and not sinners from among the Gentiles.

And we know that a person is not justified by the works of the law, but through faith in Jesus Christ. So we too have believed in Jesus Christ, in order to be justified by faith in Jesus Christ and not by the works of the law. For no flesh will be justified by the works of the law.
But if, while we seek to be justified in Christ, we ourselves are found to be sinners, has Christ then become a servant of sin? Certainly not!
For if I build up again what I tore down, I show myself to be a transgressor of the law.
For through the law I died to the law, so that I might live for God. I have been crucified with Christ.
It is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. And the life I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.
I do not set aside the grace of God. If righteousness comes through the law, then did Christ die for nothing?
O foolish Galatians, who has cast an evil eye on you? Before your very eyes I portrayed Christ as crucified.
I want to learn only this from you: did you receive the Spirit by the works of the law, or by hearing with faith?
Are you so foolish? You began in the Spirit; are you now finishing in the flesh?
Did you suffer so much for nothing? If it really was for nothing!
Does the one who gave you the Spirit and works mighty deeds among you do it by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?
Just as Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness.
Do you know, then, that those who are of faith are the children of Abraham?
For the Scripture, knowing beforehand that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, announced the good news to Abraham beforehand: "In you all the Gentiles shall be blessed."
So then, those who are of faith are blessed together with Abraham, the believer.
For all who are of the works of the law are under a curse. As it is written: "Cursed be everyone who does not continue in all that is written in the book of this law, to do it."
And that no one is justified before God by the law is [?] evident, for: "The righteous shall live by faith."
But the law is not of faith; rather, "whoever does it shall live by it."
Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law and came under a curse for us. For it is written: "Cursed be everyone who hangs on a tree."
So that the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles through Jesus Christ, so that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.
Brothers, I speak in human terms: no one sets aside a person's will once it has been ratified, or adds another provision to it.
Now the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his offspring. It does not say "to offsprings," as of many, but as of one: "and to your offspring," who is Christ.
This is what I mean: the law, which came four hundred and thirty years afterward, does not annul a covenant previously ratified by God, so as to make the promise void.
For if the inheritance were from the law, it would no longer be from the promise; but God granted it to Abraham freely through the promise.
Why then the law? Was it given because of transgressions, until the offspring should come to whom the promise had been made, ordained through angels by the hand of a mediator?
Now a mediator is not of one, but God is one.
Is the law, then, opposed to the promises of God? Certainly not! For if a law had been given that was able to give life, then righteousness would indeed have come from the law.
But the Scripture shut up everything under sin, so that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe.
Before faith came, we were held in custody under the law, shut up until the faith that was to come should be revealed.
So the law became our guardian leading to Christ, so that we might be justified by faith.
But now that faith has come, we are no longer under guardians.
For we are all children of God through faith in Jesus Christ,
for as many of us as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ.
There is no Jew nor Gentile; there is no slave nor free; there is no distinction of male nor female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
And if you are Christ's, then you are Abraham's children and heirs according to the promise.
Now this I say: as long as the heir is still a child, he is no better than a slave, though he is lord of all.
Instead he is under tutors and stewards until the coming of the appointed [?] of his father.
So it is with us too: when we were still children, we were held in bondage under the order of this world.
But when the fullness of time came, God sent his Son, who came and was born of a woman, and he was placed under the law,
so that he might redeem those who were under the law, and so that we might receive adoption as sons.
And because you are sons, God sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, by which we cry out: Abba, Father.
From now on you are no longer a slave, but a son; and if a son, then also an heir through God.
But at that time you did not know God, and you served those who were not gods.
But now you have come to know God, or rather, God has known you. How can you turn back again to that weak and poor order, which you wish to serve all over again?
You observe days and months, seasons and years.
I fear for you, that I may have laboured over you in vain.
Become as I am, for I was as you are. Brothers, I beg you. You did me no wrong.
And you know that it was through weakness of the flesh that I first preached the gospel to you;
and you did not scorn or loathe the trial in my flesh, but you received me as an angel of God, as Christ Jesus.
Where, then, is that blessedness of yours? I bear you witness that, if it had been possible, you would have torn out your eyes and given them to me.
Have I then become some kind of enemy to you because I told you the truth?
They court you zealously, but not for good; rather, they want to turn you away, so that you will imitate them.
It is good to be zealous for what is good, and not [only] when I come to you.
My children, for whom I am again in labour pains until Christ is formed among you.
I wish I could come to you now and change my tone, for I am bewildered about you.
Tell me, you who wish to be under the law, have you not read the law?
For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the slave woman and one by the free woman.
But the son of the slave woman was born according to the flesh, while the son of the free woman was born through the promise.
This is an allegory, for these are the two covenants. One is from Mount Sinai, bearing children into slavery; this is Hagar.
For Mount Sinai in Arabia corresponds to this present Jerusalem, for she is in slavery with her children.
But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother.

For it is written: "Rejoice, you barren one who does not bear; lift up your voice and cry out, you who did not have labour pains, for the children of the desolate one are more than those of her who had a husband."
But we, brothers, are children of the promise through Isaac.
But just as at that time the one born according to the flesh persecuted the one born according to the Spirit, so it is now also.
And what does the Scripture say? "Cast out that slave woman and her son, for the son of the slave woman shall not inherit with the son of the free woman."
Therefore, brothers, we are not children of the slave woman, but of the free woman.
Stand firm in the freedom with which Christ has set us free, and do not submit again to the yoke of slavery.
Look, I, Paul, tell you: if you are circumcised, Christ will be of no benefit to you.
Again I testify to every man who is circumcised that he is obliged to keep the whole law.
You who are justified by the law have been cut off from Christ; you have fallen away from grace.
For through the Spirit, by faith, we wait for the hope of righteousness.
For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any power, but faith that is helped by love.
You were running well; who hindered you so that you do not obey the truth?
That obedience does not come from the one who called you.
A little leaven leavens the whole batch of dough.
But I am confident about you in the Lord that you will think no other way; but the one who is stirring you up will bear the judgment, whoever he may be.
But I, brothers, if I am still preaching circumcision, why am I still being persecuted? Has the stumbling block of the cross been done away with?
It would be fitting if those who are troubling you were removed from you.
For you were called to freedom, brothers; only do not use that freedom as an occasion for the flesh, but through love serve one another.
For the whole law is fulfilled in one word: "You shall love your neighbour as yourself."
If you bite and devour one another, watch out that you are not destroyed by one another.
But I say this: let us walk by the Spirit, and do not carry out the desire of the flesh.
For the flesh desires against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; and these are opposed to one another, so that you do not do what you want.
If you conduct yourselves by the flesh [?], you are not under the law.
For the works of the flesh are plain, and they are: fornications, adulteries, impurities, uncleannesses,
idolatries, sorceries, enmities, quarrels, jealousies, fits of anger, factions, disturbances,
debaucheries, drunkenness, envy, murders, revelries, and things like these. I tell you about them in advance, as I told you before: those who do such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith,
gentleness, endurance. There is no law against such things.
And those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified their own flesh, with its passions and desires.
If we live by the Spirit, let us also abide by the Spirit.
Let us not be arrogant, accusing one another or envying one another.
Brothers, if someone is caught in some fault, you who are spiritual should set such a person right in a spirit of peace. Watch yourself, so that you are not tempted as well.
Bear one another's burdens, and in this way fulfil the law of Christ.
If anyone thinks he is something when he is nothing, he deceives himself.
Instead, let each person test his own works. Then he will have cause for praise in himself alone, and not in comparison with his neighbour,
for each person will carry his own load.
Let the one who is untaught share in the word of the teacher in every good thing.
Do not be deceived: God is mocked by no one. Whatever a person sows, that is what he will reap.
For whoever sows in his own flesh will reap corruption from his own flesh, but whoever sows by the Spirit will reap eternal life from the Spirit.
Let us not grow weary of doing good, for we will reap in due time if we do not give up.
So then, while we still have time, let us do good to everyone, and especially to those of the household of faith.
See what large letters I have written to you with my own hand.
Those who want to make a good showing in the flesh are the ones trying to force you to be circumcised, but only so that they do not have to follow the cross of Christ.
Not even those who are circumcised keep the law themselves. They want you to be circumcised so that they can boast about your flesh.
But far be it from me to boast of anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
From now on neither circumcision nor uncircumcision is anything; what counts is a new creation.
And peace be on those who keep to this rule, and mercy on the Israel of God.
From now on let no one cause me trouble, for I carry the sufferings of our Lord Jesus Christ in my body.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen.
